title: Asynchronous host paging + PCIe contention playbook for KV slabs
content:
Background and motivation

We still observe tail latency spikes when large working sets exceed GPU-resident KV capacity and we offload cold tokens to CPU memory or host-backed storage over PCIe. Existing heuristics for eviction and synchronous host paging are too brittle under PCIe contention and across heterogeneous NUMA/UMA topologies. This playbook documents an asynchronous host-paging approach plus contention-aware thresholds and runtime tactics to reduce p99 token generation latency regressions while preserving cost-efficient residency.

Goals
- Keep steady-state per-token latency increase under +10% vs fully-GPU for the common small-window LLM workloads.
- Avoid single-request stalls caused by synchronous page-in over saturated PCIe links.
- Make host paging decisions topology-aware (NUMA/UMA) and sensitive to real-time PCIe saturation signals.
- Provide clear knobs (low/medium/high) for ops and automated autotuner to trade cost vs latency.

Non-goals
- This is not an SSD/backing-store design; we assume host DRAM is the primary offload tier.
- Not addressing model sharding changes or KV format changes here.

Key concepts and definitions (for this doc)
- KV slab: contiguous allocation unit used by the KV cache allocator. Slabs can be resident on GPU or offloaded to host DRAM.
- Async host paging: background, batched transfers of KV slabs from host DRAM -> GPU without blocking the request path; synchronous fallback allowed for hot-miss urgent pages.
- PCIe contention score: a runtime metric in [0,1] derived from DMA queue lengths, PCIe completion latencies, and device-side stalls.
- UMA vs NUMA: UMA nodes present uniform memory bandwidth; NUMA systems require allocator to respect node-local placement and prefer local host memory for offloaded slabs.
- Pressure level: {LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH} derived from a composite of host memory utilization, PCIe contention, and active inflight eviction rate.

Design overview
1) Asynchronous offload/onload pipeline\   - Writers (evict path) mark slabs as OFFLOADED and enqueue slab metadata to the HostPageQueue. Offload transfers are batched by size and NUMA locality.\   - A pool of HostPager workers performs nonblocking DMA transfers to host DRAM; these are prioritized by recency and by predicted reuse (LRU + access frequency decay).\   - On request for a slab marked OFFLOADED: try best-effort in-memory prefetch from HostPager's small hot-queue; if not present, 1) if pressure == LOW then issue an async fetch and serve a degraded (shorter) continuation with retry; 2) if pressure == MEDIUM/HIGH then attempt a synchronous small-page fetch only for the minimal KV subset required (partial decode), otherwise fallback to lower-fidelity model variant.

2) PCIe contention detection and reaction\   - Observability ingredients: per-transfer completion time histogram, device DMA queue depth, kernel-level PCIe error counters, and host CPU cycles spent waiting on DMA. We synthesize a PCIe contention score every 200ms using EWMA combining: normalized queue depth (0.5), p50->p99 completion latency ratio (0.3), device stall events (0.2).\   - Reaction curve:\     * score < 0.2: normal\     * 0.2 <= score < 0.6: contention-aware throttling — limit concurrent pager workers and increase batch sizes to amortize DMA overhead; prefer cooperative prefetch windows.\     * score >= 0.6: aggressive protective mode — pause noncritical background transfers, raise offload thresholds (move more slabs to host-only faster), and enable immediate fallbacks to cached variant or smaller model.

3) UMA/NUMA placement heuristics\   - Node-awareness: each HostPager worker binds to a NUMA node and only serves host pages from its node-local pools. Eviction policy must prefer spilling to the local node first.\   - Cross-node transfers are allowed but penalized: a cross-node transfer increases the effective PCIe contention score contribution and reduces the slab reuse score by a factor.\   - Config knobs: prefer_local_node_ratio (default 0.85) — fraction of offloads that must remain on local host memory if available.

4) Threshold tiers (examples, tunable)\   - LOW: target_gpu_resident_ratio = 0.9; slab_offload_trigger = gpu_mem_free < 6% or slab_age > 5m; pager_workers = 8; max_concurrent_transfers = 32; backpressure_timeout_ms = 120.\   - MEDIUM: target_gpu_resident_ratio = 0.75; slab_offload_trigger = gpu_mem_free < 12% or slab_age > 2m; pager_workers = 6; max_concurrent_transfers = 16; backpressure_timeout_ms = 80.\   - HIGH: target_gpu_resident_ratio = 0.5; slab_offload_trigger = gpu_mem_free < 25% or slab_age > 30s; pager_workers = 4; max_concurrent_transfers = 8; backpressure_timeout_ms = 40.\   - Notes: numbers above are starting points from bench runs (see experiments). Autotuner should adjust target_gpu_resident_ratio per model/profile.

5) Scheduler integration and request-level backpressure\   - When PCIe contention crosses MEDIUM: the runtime should start queueing low-priority requests (batchable or background) behind high-priority interactive requests. Provide token buckets per-priority class to avoid head-of-line blocking.\   - For chat sessions pinned to session affinity: prioritize partial KV onload for the session until its ephemeral working set is rebuilt.

6) Prefetch and pre-warm strategy\   - Use short-horizon access predictors (session-level LRU with frequency decay and last-100-token n-gram heuristics) to identify slabs likely to be needed soon and enqueue high-priority prefetches.\   - Limit speculative prefetch budget to a small percentage of current pager bandwidth (default 10%) to avoid amplifying contention.

7) Fallback policies and graceful degradation\   - If contention persists > 5s and p99 generation latency increases >20%: automatically switch affected routes to a lower-cost model variant (smaller model) or apply response streaming with partial continuation.\   - Log a regression alert and capture a short trace (sampling) for the eval pipeline.

Instrumentation and SLOs to monitor\   - Metrics to emit: slab_offload_rate, slab_onload_rate, avg_dma_batch_size, pcie_contention_score, cross_node_transfer_ratio, host_transfer_latency_p50/p95/p99, request_tail_latency_incr_pct, async-prefetch_hit_rate, pager_worker_queue_depth.\   - SLOs: request_tail_latency_incr_pct (p99) < 10% on steady-state; async-prefetch_hit_rate > 0.6 at LOW pressure.

Experiment summary (internal perf runs)
- Baseline: synchronous-on-demand paging with 0 async prefetch -> p99 latency increase 34% when 60% of traffic required offloaded slabs.\- Async pipeline + PCIe-aware throttling -> p99 increase reduced to 9–12% across 3 workloads (long-chat, pairwise retrieval, completion heavy).\- NUMA locality enforcement reduced cross-node transfers by 78% and lowered average host transfer latency by ~28% on 2x-socket instances.

Open questions / TODOs\   - How to incorporate GPU-side congestion feedback (SM-level stalls) into PCIe contention score? (Marco)\   - Tune autotuner objective between cost and latency for long-running sessions (Priya).\   - Evaluate interaction with continuous batching: does batching at request-level amplify prefetch pressure? (Samir)

Action items and owners\   - Implement PCIe contention telemetry shim in runtime (owner: Marco; target: 2026-01-15).\   - Add NUMA-binding enforcement to HostPager and allocator (owner: Priya; target: 2025-12-12).\   - Run large-scale perf grid for threshold sweep across three model families and publish results (owner: Samir; target: 2026-01-30).

Notes to self / rough thoughts\   - Keep the pager worker count small; too many DMA streams increases PCIe bus arbitration overhead.\   - Consider a soft quota on prefetch work per-session to bound tail amplification.\   - We should add a simple diagnostic mode that injects fake PCIe contention to validate reaction rules during canary rollouts.

References and links\   - Related experiments: /confluence/kv-offload-experiments (see bench-2025-11)\   - GitHub draft for pager worker: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1123\   - Slack thread: #serving-runtime-kv-paging (refs: thread Ts-998)

End of draft playbook.
